“One Minutes” (15 per side)

Begin Consideration of H.Res. 1247 – Providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 2102) to amend title 10, United States Code, to provide for concurrent receipt of veterans' disability compensation and retired pay for disability retirees with combat-related disabilities, and for other purposes (Rep. Takano's Discharge Petition) (Rep. Takano – Rules) – VOTE YES

H.R. 1013 – Retirement Fairness for Charities and Educational Institutions Act of 2025 (Rep. Lucas – Financial Services) (Subject to a Rule)

This bill allows banks, investment companies, and investment professionals to offer unregistered insurance contracts and collective investment trusts (CITs) to 403(b) plans. Such retirement plans, collectively holding more than $1 trillion in retirement nest eggs, are commonly offered to public school teachers and administrators, non-profit professionals, church employees, and some healthcare workers. 

Currently, federal securities laws require those who offer annuities and mutual funds to 403(b) plans to register with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) as a broker-dealer or investment advisor. That registration subjects both sellers and products to SEC oversight, including fiduciary-duty and Regulation Best Interest. This bill would eliminate those requirements for these products, undermining consumer protections such as disclosing or limiting conflicts of interest. 

Additionally, many of the individuals impacted by this bill are employed by smaller organizations or institutions with limited tools to examine complex retirement portfolios. This means that state guardrails – which vary widely and can be difficult to enforce – may be the only protections left in place for those who have dedicated their careers to the communities around them.

Ranking Member Waters voted against this bill in Committee.

The Rule, which was adopted yesterday, provides for one hour of debate equally divided and controlled by the Chair and Ranking Member of the Committee on Financial Services or their respective designees.

Complete Consideration of H.R. 9237 – Take Care of America’s Veterans Act (Rep. Bost – Veterans' Affairs) (Subject to a Rule) – VOTE NO

This bill purports to increase benefits for veterans and improve services offered by the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA). In reality, it would undercut critical care and benefits for those who have dedicated their lives to serving this country.  

House Republicans have chosen to put forward a bill with no input or buy-in from House Democrats that hijacks bipartisan priorities while advancing their own partisan policy provisions. These provisions will undercut the VA care and benefits veterans rely on day-to-day. While House Democrats are working to ensure veterans have easy access to their disability benefits and treatment options, cutting certain benefits for one group of veterans to fund new benefits for another is not the answer. Unfortunately, this bill does exactly that – cutting future benefits for 1.5 million veterans with tinnitus and sleep apnea to cover the cost of benefits for other veterans. Those savings do not come from waste or bureaucracy. They come directly from veterans.

The bill also contains large fee increases to VA home loan programs that veterans rely on for their housing needs. Ultimately, this bill would slash approximately $57 billion over the next 10 years in veterans earned disability compensation and $4 billion in home loan benefits and is opposed by a wide coalition – including several Veteran Service Organizations. 

House Democrats have led a successful bipartisan discharge petition that would bring the Major Richard Star Act to the Floor, which would ensure medically retired veterans receive their full Department of Defense retirement pay and their full VA disability pay without cutting the benefits of other veterans. House Republicans should join this effort to advance the needs of the veteran community – without harming it in the process.

Ranking Member Takano strongly opposes this bill.

The Rule, which was adopted on Tuesday, July 14, 2026, provides for no further debate.

  4. H.R. 10353 – SBIC Reporting Modernization Act of 2026 (Rep. Finstad – Small Business)
  5. H.R. 10238 – Cybersecurity for Small Businesses Act of 2026, as amended (Rep. Wied – Small Business)
  6. H.R. 9718 – Reshoring American Manufacturing Act of 2026, as amended (Rep. Wied – Small Business)
  7. H.R. 10375 – 504 Modernization and Small Manufacturer Enhancement Act of 2026, as amended (Rep. Velázquez – Small Business)

  1. H.R. 5549 – Efficient Nuclear Licensing Hearings Act (Rep. Griffith – Energy and Commerce)
  2. H.R. 9084 – Department of Energy Nuclear Transparency Act, as amended (Rep. Castor – Energy and Commerce)
